transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess I've just been getting kind of stuck on... on this spot on my face. It's just this tiny, uneven area around my nose and cheek. I just... I see it a lot in photos, and under the really bright lights at the store where I work. Other people say they don't even see it, but... I don't know. It just feels like it's the first thing customers and managers notice about me.
Is this concern about the spot on your face affecting your daily life or work in any way?

Um... I guess a little. My manager... well, they noticed I've been coming back from my breaks late recently. And that I'm kind of moving slower at the register. I just... I'm worried it's making me look unreliable. Especially right now, since I'm trying to get promoted... so it's just not great.
Do you think the spot on your face is actually there, or is it something you're just worried about?
Um... I mean, I see it. So... it's there. But... I don't know. I guess maybe I just focus on it more than I should. I'm not really sure.
Has your perception of the spot on your face changed at all over time?
Um... not really, I guess. I mean... it's just always kind of been the same. I just notice it.
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about the spot on your face?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, that's kind of why I came in. I just... I keep getting stuck on it. It's this tiny uneven spot, mostly around my nose and cheek. I just... I see it in photos, and under those bright store lights at work. And... even when people say they don't see it, it just feels like it's the first thing customers and my managers notice when they look at me. So... yeah, it's hard to stop thinking about it.
How much distress does thinking about the spot on your face cause you?
Um... I don't really know. It's... I mean, it just bothers me. I'm not sure if I'd call it distress, exactly. It's just... annoying, I guess.
Has your concern about the spot on your face caused you to avoid any social or work-related activities?

Um... not exactly avoid, no. But... I guess it's been affecting work a little bit. Like, I've been taking longer in the bathroom on my breaks to check my face, so... I've been coming back late. And I guess I'm just... a bit slower at the register lately because I'm distracted. My manager brought it up. It just sucks because... I'm really trying to get promoted, and I'm worried this is just making me look... unreliable.
Is it specifically the spot on your face that you're worried about, or is it more about what others might think of you in general?

Um... no, I think it's really just the spot. Like I said before, I just... I get stuck on that one uneven part by my nose. I don't really worry too much about what people think of me in general. It's just... I know that's the first thing the customers and my managers see when they look at me under those lights. So... yeah. Just the spot.
Do you think you would still be bothered by the spot on your face if nobody else ever noticed it?
Um... I don't know. I guess... I haven't really thought about it like that. It's just... it's there, you know? I don't know if it matters if anyone else sees it. I just... I don't like it.
Do you think there's anything that could be done to fix the spot on your face that would make you stop worrying about it?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... I don't know what would actually fix it. I just... I haven't really figured that out. I just wish it wasn't there.
Do you think you could ever come to accept the spot on your face as it is, without feeling the need to change it?
I don't... I mean, I don't think so. I just... I can't really imagine just being okay with it. It's just... I just want it gone.
Do you believe that if the spot on your face were to disappear, your life or work situation would significantly improve?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it changing my whole life or anything. I just work at a register, so... I don't think my job would really change. I just... maybe I'd feel a little better. But I'm not sure.
Is your main concern about the spot on your face because of how it looks to you or because of how you think it makes you appear to others?

Um... I guess it's both. I mean, I see it all the time... like in photos, or when I'm working under those bright store lights. It's just this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek, but I get stuck on it. And... I know other people say they don't see it, but... it feels like it's the first thing customers notice when I'm at the register. Or my managers. It just feels really obvious to me.
Do you think you would still see the spot on your face as a problem if a doctor or a dermatologist told you that it was completely normal and not noticeable to others?
I don't know... I mean, people already tell me they don't see it. So... I guess even if a doctor said that, I'd probably still feel the same way. It's just... I still see it.
Do you think there is any possibility that the spot on your face could be less noticeable than you think it is?
I mean... maybe? I don't know. It's hard to say. I just... I see it. So it feels noticeable to me.
Do you think your concern about the spot on your face might decrease if you were able to ignore it or distract yourself from thinking about it?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess maybe, if I could actually stop thinking about it. But... I don't really know. I haven't really been able to just ignore it.
Do you think there's anything that could change your mind about how the spot on your face looks?
I don't know. I can't really think of anything. I mean... it's just there. So... probably not.
Do you think there's anything that could convince you that the spot on your face is not as noticeable as you think it is?
Um... I don't really think so. Like... even if someone told me they couldn't see it, I still have to look at it. So... I don't really know what would convince me otherwise.
Do you think the spot on your face would still be there if you couldn't see yourself in a mirror or in photos?
Um... I guess so? I mean... I don't really know. It's on my face, so... yeah, it would still be there. I just wouldn't be looking at it. But... I'm not really sure how to answer that.
